prompt:
Extract every policy commitment stated in the text below.

Rules:
- One commitment per line.
- Write each as a verb phrase: an action followed by its object. For example: "raise the income tax threshold" or "build 300000 new homes".
- State each commitment at the level of a distinct policy action, not its implementation details. Do not subdivide a single commitment into steps.
- Include every commitment. Do not select, rank, prioritise, or judge importance.
- Use the text's own terms for policy objects. Do not substitute synonyms.
- Do not number the lines. No bullets, headings, preamble, or commentary.
- If the text states no policy commitments, output the single word NONE.

<text>
Summary of proposals

Economy, tax, and spending
- Cut £12bn in annual government spending by 2007–08 via reduced bureaucracy, a civil service recruitment freeze, abolishing/quango cuts, and regulatory reform.
- Use £8bn of these savings to reduce borrowing and £4bn for tax cuts in the first Budget.
- Limit overall spending growth to 4% annually to 2011–12; maintain Bank of England independence; no entry to the Euro.
- Halve council tax bills for many pensioner households (up to £500), link the basic state pension to earnings, retain existing pensioner benefits.
- Create Lifetime Savings Accounts with government top-ups; encourage “opt-out” workplace pensions; use unclaimed financial assets to help failed pension schemes.
- Reduce regulation via departmental “regulatory budgets,” cost–benefit tests, sunset reviews, and ending “gold-plating” of EU directives; seek restoration of the UK opt-out from the EU Social Chapter.

Families, childcare, and education
- More flexible maternity pay (option of higher pay over six months or lower over nine).
- Up to £50 per week per under-5 for eligible working families regardless of childcare type; support workplace nurseries; new clubs for older children.
- Additional £15bn annually for schools by 2009–10; simplify school funding so money follows the pupil.
- Strengthen discipline by giving heads control over admissions/expulsions; establish Turnaround Schools for disruptive pupils; reduce teacher paperwork.
- Increase exam transparency (publish marks), allow international qualifications, slim the National Curriculum, and prioritise vocational routes with 300,000 grants for 14–16-year-olds.
- Two hours of after-school sport per week; ban junk food in schools; support school trips.
- Expand popular schools (600,000 new places first term); allow free places at independent schools where costs match state funding.
- Moratorium on closing special schools; reform further education funding and allow “super college” status; scrap university tuition fees and the admissions regulator; grow university endowments.

Health and social care
- Increase NHS funding to about £2,000 per head; abolish central targets; reduce PCTs and abolish Strategic Health Authorities; cut quangos/inspectorates.
- Funding to follow patients; greater hospital autonomy; “bring back matron,” create infection-control teams, expand single rooms, and allow community hospitals to remain where locally supported.
- Offer a contribution (half the NHS tariff) to patients who self-pay for operations; expand social care choice and protect against forced home sales; more respite for carers.
- Reform dentistry payments and offer low monthly plans; health checks for long-stay non-EU migrants; public campaign on STIs.

Crime, justice, and security
- Recruit 5,000 additional police officers per year; cut paperwork; introduce elected police commissioners; focus on neighbourhood policing.
- End early release; add 20,000 prison places; require offenders to serve stated minimum terms.
- Expand drug treatment with 25,000 residential places; require treatment or court; reclassify cannabis to Class B.
- Appoint a Homeland Security Minister; strengthen counter-terror laws and coordination.

Immigration and borders
- Establish a British Border Control Police; restore embarkation controls; 24-hour port surveillance.
- Adopt an Australian-style points system for work permits.
- Set an annual limit for overall immigration, including a fixed refugee quota; process asylum claims outside the UK; take a set share from UNHCR.
- Seek national control over asylum policy and modernised international agreements.

Governance and communities
- Publish a delivery timetable and tie ministerial roles to performance.
- Abolish regional assemblies; return planning, housing, transport, and fire powers to local authorities; strengthen Parliament; reduce MPs by 20%; ensure “English votes for English laws.”
- Wales referendum on Assembly powers; uphold consent-based approach in Northern Ireland.
- Devolve planning; act against illegal traveller encampments; extend Right to Buy to housing association tenants and expand shared ownership.
- Transport: modernise roads; review speed cameras; lengthen rail franchises.
- Environment: protect Green Belt, focus development on brownfield sites, phase out HFCs, incentivise low-emission cars, increase recycling, support renewables and efficiency for energy security.
- Agriculture and rural: honest food labelling; support local food; require public food procurement to meet British standards; pursue CAP reform; update animal welfare; free vote to overturn the hunting ban.

Foreign and defence
- Increase frontline defence spending by £2.7bn by 2007–08; retain regiments; improve procurement; keep key warships; support service families; keep NATO central.
- Remain engaged in Iraq reconstruction; support a two-state outcome in the Middle East.
- Oppose the EU Constitution and Euro; seek Social Chapter opt-out; repatriate fisheries control; back EU enlargement including Turkey.
- Target 0.7% of national income for aid by 2013; seek more national control of aid spending.

Immediate actions promised
- Start recruiting 5,000 extra police per year; reintroduce matrons; first Budget to cut waste and reduce taxes; empower heads to expel disruptive pupils; begin 24-hour port surveillance; set a referendum date on the EU Constitution.
